knowledge:
- key_parameters: negativeCon=Character string specifying the negative control siRNA name in the EXPERIMENT_TYPE column ;; positiveCon=Character string specifying the positive control siRNA name in the EXPERIMENT_TYPE column ;; useMean=Logical parameter in zFactor to use mean (default) or median (if FALSE) for robust calculation ;; control_name=Vector of control siRNA names to plot in scatterPlot ;; normMethod=Normalization method or control siRNA used for normalization in madSelect, siRNAPlot, and rsaHits ;; LB=Lower bound parameter for rsaHits (default 0.2) ;; UB=Upper bound parameter for rsaHits (default 0.8) ;; revHits=Logical parameter in rsaHits to reverse hit selection direction ;; Bonferroni=Logical parameter in rsaHits to apply Bonferroni correction ;; outputFile=Character string specifying the output CSV file name for RSA results
- alternatives: The package itself implements and compares four alternative hit selection methods: Student's t-test (on robust B-scores), Median ± k MAD, Rank Products, and Redundant siRNA Activity (RSA). RSA is preferred when multiple siRNAs target a single gene to reduce off-target effects.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-throughput synthetic lethal RNAi screen data where two identical cell lines (one with a gene knocked down, one control) are screened to identify genes that lead to stronger knock-down effects (higher mortality) under treatment compared to control.
- pitfalls: The input data.table must contain exactly 8 mandatory columns (PLATE, MASTER_PLATE, WELL_CONTENT_NAME, EXPERIMENT_TYPE, EXPERIMENT_MODIFICATION, ROW_NAME, COL_NAME, and READOUT) with exact names; changing these column names will cause errors. Shuffled or randomized readout data will yield negative Z and Z' factors. Off-target effects are common in RNAi screens; the documentation warns that siRNA hits picked by different algorithms may vary, and recommends verifying genes that show significant knock-down effects in at least two siRNAs.

workflows.name: synthetic_lethal_rnai_screen_analysis
workflows.intent: Process synthetic lethal RNAi screen data, perform quality control, visualize results, and identify hit genes using multiple statistical methods.
input: screen_results.csv (A table containing RNAi screen results with mandatory columns: PLATE, MASTER_PLATE, WELL_CONTENT_NAME, EXPERIMENT_TYPE, EXPERIMENT_MODIFICATION, ROW_NAME, COL_NAME, and READOUT)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and data ;; 2. Calculate Z and Z' factors for quality control ;; 3. Visualize screen data using heatmaps and scatter plots ;; 4. Plot knock-down effects for individual genes of interest ;; 5. Calculate robust B-scores and perform Student's t-test ;; 6. Perform hit selection using Median ± k MAD ;; 7. Perform hit selection using Rank Products ;; 8. Perform hit selection using Redundant siRNA Activity (RSA)
workflows.code:
library(synlet)
data(example_dt)
head(example_dt)
res <- zFactor(example_dt, negativeCon = "scrambled control si1", positiveCon = "PLK1 si1")
head(res)
plateHeatmap(example_dt)
scatterPlot(example_dt, controlOnly = FALSE, control_name = c("PLK1 si1", "scrambled control si1", "lipid only"))
zF_mean <- zFactor(example_dt, negativeCon = "scrambled control si1", positiveCon = "PLK1 si1")
zF_med <- zFactor(example_dt, negativeCon = "scrambled control si1", positiveCon = "PLK1 si1", useMean = FALSE)
siRNAPlot("AAK1", example_dt,
           controlsiRNA = c("lipid only", "scrambled control si1"),
           FILEPATH = ".",  zPrimeMed = zF_med, zPrimeMean = zF_mean,
           treatment = "treatment", control = "control",
           normMethod = c("PLATE", "lipid only", "scrambled control si1"))
bscore_res <- sapply(unique(example_dt$MASTER_PLATE)[1], bScore, example_dt, treatment = "treatment", control = "control", simplify = FALSE)
head(bscore_res$P001)
t_res <- tTest(bscore_res$P001, 3, 3)
head(t_res)
mad_res <- sapply((unique(example_dt$MASTER_PLATE)),
                  madSelect,
                  example_dt,
                  control   = "control",
                  treatment = "treatment",
                  simplify  = FALSE)
head(mad_res$P001)
rp_res <- sapply(unique(example_dt$MASTER_PLATE),
                 rankProdHits,
                 example_dt,
                 control   = "control",
                 treatment = "treatment",
                 simplify  = FALSE)
head(rp_res)
rsaHits(example_dt, treatment = "treatment", control = "control",
        normMethod = "PLATE", LB = 0.2, UB = 0.8, revHits = FALSE,
        Bonferroni = FALSE, outputFile = "RSAhits.csv")
